article_title: psqlODBC 18.00.0006 Fixes Vulnerabilities Including an SQL Injection in SQLSpecialColumns and Several Buffer Overflows; All Earlier Releases Affected

content_preview.title: psqlODBC 18.00.0006 Fixes Vulnerabilities Including an SQL Injection in SQLSpecialColumns and Several Buffer Overflows; All Earlier Releases Affected
content_preview.summary: The PostgreSQL ODBC project released psqlODBC 18.00.0006 on November 2; its changelog lists CVE-2026-120057 through CVE-2026-120067 and says all earlier releases are affected.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The PostgreSQL ODBC project announced a security release for psqlODBC on 2026-11-02. According to the [PostgreSQL news archive](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/security-release-for-psqlodbc-3431/), the project "has released version 18.00.0006 to fix multiple security issues" and points readers to the changelog for details. The [project's GitHub release tag page](https://github.com/postgresql-interfaces/psqlodbc/releases/tag/REL-18_00_0006) carries a release titled psqlODBC 18....

editor_notes.content_quality: Compact Briefing (474 words, within the 300-800 range) with a clear structure: announcement, changelog CVE list split by rating, non-CVE hardening, preceding release, and a 'What We Don't Know' section. The title is 149 characters, under the 150-character threshold.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk (source-0/1/2.html.gz) and cross-checked the changelog against the raw Changelog.md fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com. source-0 (postgresql.org news, posted 2026-11-02 by Postgresql ODBC): quoted text 'has released version 18.00.0006 to fix multiple security issues' appears verbatim, followed by 'see the Changelog for details'; confirms the date and the pointer to the changelog. source-1 (project Changelog.md): '## 18.00.0006' section contains the quoted sentence 'This release fixes the following vulnerabilities. All releases before 18.00.0006 are affected.' verbatim; lists exactly 11 CVEs, CVE-2026-120057 through CVE-2026-120067, each with a GHSA ID and CVSS 3.1 rating. Independent recount from the raw text: High = 120057 (7.5), 120058 (7.5), 120061 (7.5), 120062 (7.5), 120064 (7.5), 120065 (7.1) = 6; Medium = 120059 (6.8), 120060 (5.9), 120063 (5.9), 120066 (5.3), 120067 (5.9) = 5. The Herald's own count of 'six High, five Medium' is correct and every score and description in the article matches. Three entries (120059, 120060, 120065) are described in terms of server-supplied data, as stated. The hardening paragraph quotes 'They have no demonstrated attack path and no CVE.' verbatim; there are exactly four bullets and the article's summary of each (SQLSetDescRecW freed buffer / local variable address, SQLColumns uninitialized relkind and OID, convert_linefeeds NULL dereference in one build configuration, secure_sscanf / msgtowstr / MSDTC bounds) matches. The 18.00.0005 entry (heap corruption when binding more than 32767 parameters, GHSA-cmfx-rm3r-p2jr) matches. 'Does not say whether exploited / no mitigations described' holds: the changelog has no exploitation or workaround text for this release (the one 'exploit' hit is old, unrelated holdable-cursor text). source-2 (GitHub release page REL-18_00_0006): release titled 'psqlODBC 18.00.0006', released 02 Nov by davecramer on commit 96fa03d; it carries no release notes body, which the article does not claim otherwise. Source type: all three are the project's own first-party pages (PostgreSQL project news, project changelog, project release tag); there is no independent coverage, which is acceptable for a Briefing and is disclosed by the article's sourcing. suspicious_patterns was null for all three sources. Domains github.com and postgresql.org are on the allowlist.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, CVE ID, CVSS value, date, version and quote traced to the snapshots; no discrepancies. Title claims (SQL injection in SQLSpecialColumns, several buffer overflows, all earlier releases affected) are supported by CVE-2026-120062, the overflow entries 120057/120058/120061/120063/120067, and the 'All releases before 18.00.0006 are affected' sentence. Summary matches the sources. The 'by the Herald's own count' labels are accurate and correctly marked as the Herald's tally.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; no sensational wording, no AI self-reference, no speculation about exploitation.
editor_notes.originality: No existing psqlODBC coverage in src/content/articles. Related but distinct prior coverage exists (PostgreSQL JDBC 42.7.14 CVEs, pgvector 0.8.7 CVE); different projects and releases, no overlap.
concerns: First-party-only sourcing: all three sources are the psqlODBC/PostgreSQL project's own pages, so claims about severity rest on the project's own CVSS ratings. Acceptable for a Briefing; the article attributes ratings to the changelog.
The linked GitHub security advisories (GHSA IDs) were not cited as sources, so per-issue technical detail is not covered; the article discloses this in 'What We Don't Know'.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-scoped Briefing on a multi-CVE security release of a widely used database driver. Every claim verified against raw source text, the Herald's own High/Medium recount confirmed, no corrections needed. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate security-release coverage for the PostgreSQL/ODBC developer audience; first-party sourced and not broadly significant
